title: Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving
objective: I can model and solve real-world problems using equations and inequalities.
model: story to model: equation for an exact value, inequality for a limit; define the variable, solve, check reasonableness

widgets.root: Identical to the config warm-up (8-6 skill); keys verified.

widgets.component: choose the model for a story, solve it, check it is reasonable (4n = 52 gives 13 notebooks per box)
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (p + 12 = 45, 3 + h > 8, 31 + p ≤ 48, r ≤ 180, f = 15, d − 7 < 5, 43; r ÷ 5 = 40 gives 200, 17 + b ≤ 30 gives b ≤ 13, 7k = 3.5 gives 0.5, 6w = 3.6 not 21.6). Challenge 2.4 tape viz shows 17, b and the total 30.
Bins verified, including 'The temperature must stay above 32 degrees' (inequality) and 'The code is exactly 24 digits long' (equation). This is the lesson's central decision.

widgets.component: wrong inverse, wrong model: 'at most 200' modelled as exactly 66, 'no more than 8' as p = 8, 'split equally' as ≥, multiplied instead of divided
widgets.root: Error step indices match; each fault is an equation-versus-inequality or inverse-operation error that the lesson names.

widgets.component: which equation or inequality models the story
widgets.root: Keys verified in 7 seeds each (8n = 16, s ÷ 9 = 5, 56 + m ≤ 92); distractors reverse the operands (9 ÷ s = 5) or swap the symbol family.

widgets.component: 'How many pages are left?', 'How many more dollars does Kenji need?' with a single numeric answer
widgets.root: In the sampled seeds 4 of 7 L3 slots and 3 of 7 L4 slots are two-step subtraction word problems (63 − 18 − 33 = 12, 67 − 17 − 15 = 35) with no unknown, no limit and no equation or inequality to write. The prompt 'Write an equation, then solve it' is on some, but only the number is graded. They do not exercise the objective, modeling.
widgets.replacement: Make every numeric slot a two-part item: part 1 a model-choice (equation or inequality, four options built from the story's own numbers), part 2 the numeric answer, graded only if part 1 is right. Remove the template that has no unknown or no limit (running-total and 'pages left' forms), and keep the 'least whole number' inequality forms ('at least $106 at $8 each gives 14').

widgets.component: balance scale on a story equation
widgets.root: Real manipulable for the equation half. The inequality half of the lesson has no manipulable in this studio (no act:ineq), which the sort and error items partly cover.

widgets.component: solve four models (12f = 96, t − 9 = 15, c ÷ 6 = 14, 17 + b ≤ 30), write your own pair of problems
'Why is one an equation and the other an inequality?' with a flashlight answer
widgets.root: 'One' and 'the other' point at 5.1 (320 + r ≤ 500) and 5.2 (4f = 60), and the flashlight story is not on screen. Out of sequence the item cannot be answered.
widgets.replacement: State both models in the stem: 'Lena models the cost limit as 320 + r ≤ 500 and the cost of 4 flashlights at an exact price as 4f = 60. Why is the first an inequality and the second an equation?' with the flashlight story in one sentence above.

typography: Practice 2.1 (choice p / 12 = 45) and 2.3 (stem and explanation 'n / 6 = 7', 'Divided by 6 is n / 6') print division as a spaced slash instead of ÷
